[Discussion] Is it beneficial for MMO games to start out small?

I would say it could be useful to establish core game mechanics and balance things out early with a small group of players who have the patience to let the developers do their thing without bitching and spreading negative feedback. Games like H1z1 that go big fast before core mechanics are sorted out (like base building) suffer a drop off of players and wind up with a lot of negative chatter associated with them on the net because people's expectations are high for games that sell big.

Also, the bigger the game, the more attractive it is to cheaters. Going big before the dev team is ready for the endless cat and mouse game of foiling cheaters is another way to turn people off your game in large numbers. This depends on the game too, some game styles are easier to detect cheating on than others but generally I think it's safe to say cheaters are bad for the game.

Being able to detect cheats is really hard in some games. Funnily enough, it's a huge problem in online chess. It's basically completely up to the players to be honest. A cheater will simply play a mirror game vs. Difficult AI and copy the moves. There's nothing anyone could do about that.
